verdict.line: You lose if you let Apprehend (E) land and Hemorrhage stack to max before you can disengage; you win if you bait it, punish its 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s cooldown, and never trade inside his hook range for free.

brief.thesis: Irelia holds the real edge here — 51.9% win rate over 646 games, lane-advantage tag — because her E stun and Q dash-reset let her dictate when fights happen, while Darius's whole kit needs you inside his 535-range Apprehend to function. The matchup is decided by whether he lands that pull: every stack of Hemorrhage he gets for free brings him closer to the enrage threshold and a lethal Noxian Guillotine.

tell.watch: Darius's Hemorrhage stack count on you

theirWindow.when: Apprehend (E) is up and you're inside 535 range
theirWindow.what: He pulls you in, gets free autos plus Q (Decimate) sweetspot to stack Hemorrhage fast, then W (Crippling Strike) slows you so you can't leave before he enrages at 5 stacks.

yourWindow.when: His E just missed or is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Walk up and commit — Q (Bladesurge) in, E (Flawless Duet) for the stun and Mark, then Q again for the free-reset since Bladesurge refreshes on a Marked target. He has no gap-closer to punish your dash back out.

start.why: The sustain and early trade damage keep you healthy through his Q (Decimate) sweetspot pokes and passive bleed ticks before you have any real itemization.

boots.why: Darius's damage is almost entirely physical autos and Q/W — flat physical reduction blunts his all-in far more than Mercury's Treads would here.

core.why: The on-hit sustain lets you out-heal his bleed stacks in extended trades, which is exactly what wins this matchup at 58.9% over 112 games.
Scales your split-push and 1v1 pressure once his E is on a long cooldown and can't threaten you back.
Turns his burst — including the enrage-boosted autos and R — into damage over time you can heal through with BotRK's lifesteal.

situational.when: you're ahead and want to end skirmishes before he stacks Hemorrhage at all
their whole team is physical damage-heavy and you need the resist alongside on-hit
he's snowballed and his R threatens to one-shot you off a single Apprehend

runes.keystoneWhy: Your Q-E dash-and-stun combo lands multiple hits fast, stacking Conqueror quickly, and its adaptive healing is what lets you win extended trades against his stacking bleed instead of losing the war of attrition.

summoners.why: Ignite denies the healing from his Q (Decimate) hitting champions and turns your all-in windows, once his E is down, into kill pressure instead of just a good trade.

playing.title: Bait Apprehend before trading
playing.detail: Stand just outside 535 range while last-hitting so he either wastes E on nothing or has to walk up without his displacement tool ready.

playing.title: Punish the E cooldown window
playing.detail: The moment his Apprehend is used or whiffs, its cooldown is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s — that's your green light to walk up and commit the full Q-E-Q combo.

playing.title: Track your own bleed stacks
playing.detail: Hemorrhage stacks up to 5 and enrages him with massive bonus Attack Damage at max — disengage before you hit that cap, not after.

playing.title: Hold W for his all-in swing
playing.detail: Defiant Dance (W) reduces physical damage taken while charging, so time the charge right as he winds up Q or commits autos in a dive.

playing.title: Land E before you dash in
playing.detail: Flawless Duet's stun and Mark set up a clean, safe Bladesurge (Q) reset and take away his chance to land Crippling Strike (W) on you first.

playing.title: Respect the R timer post-6
playing.detail: Noxian Guillotine is true damage that scales with your Hemorrhage stacks and refreshes on a kill — don't extend fights while you're bled up near his level-6+ spike.

playing.title: Win the long game, not the burst
playing.detail: Once BotRK is online and your E is closer to its 10s floor cooldown, sustained fights swing hard in your favor over his single burst windows.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners and win rates are pulled from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (646-game sample for this matchup); the tactical reasoning around cooldown windows and Hemorrhage stacking is my own read, not measured data.
